answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost.
